sources.entry: Utter - On-device voice dictation and meeting transcription powered by whisper.cpp and Metal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/h3x-levi/Utter) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Utter is a free, open-source macOS app for on-device voice dictation and meeting transcription, using whisper.cpp and a bundled speech model that works offline.
summary.what_it_does: Hold the fn key (or another modifier key) in any app, speak, and release; Utter transcribes locally and types the text at the cursor. Double-tapping fn gives hands-free dictation and Esc cancels. A Library organizes dictations, notes and meetings by day, with search, copy, re-paste and undo for deletes. Meeting mode can record the microphone and call audio from Zoom, Teams, FaceTime, Webex, Slack or Discord and label the speakers "You" and "Others". Personal vocabulary (Dictionary), text expansion Snippets with date/time/clipboard placeholders, and voice commands on selected text are included. The README also describes an optional companion robot and two speech engines: Accurate (Whisper small.en, bundled) and Fast (Whistle, bundled).
use_cases: offline voice dictation on a Mac
dictate emails and messages into any app
transcribe meeting and call audio locally
expand short phrases into longer text
how_to_run: Download Utter-1.2.0.dmg from the releases page and open it.
Open Utter and grant Microphone and Accessibility permissions.
To build: git clone the repository, cd Utter, then run swift build.
To make the app bundle: bash scripts/build-app.sh --no-dmg (builds build/Utter.app).
stack: Apple Intelligence on-device model (optional, for voice commands)
notable: Speech is processed entirely on the Mac; audio is not uploaded and there is no account, analytics or telemetry
Meeting transcription labels your microphone as "You" and call audio as "Others"
Snippets and Dictionary let you define custom expansions and spellings
Designed as a native menu-bar app with a cassette-tape-themed Library
Free and open source under Apache 2.0
caveats: Signed but not notarized, so macOS requires manually allowing the first launch via Privacy & Security
Building from source requires macOS 26 and Xcode 26, though the app runs on macOS 14 and later
The Fast engine's Whistle option is listed for Apple silicon on macOS 26; voice commands need Apple Intelligence
